info.title: THRØ API
info.description: Routes over the command handlers. One command endpoint (ADR-007); identity from the principal, never the body (ADR-008); every relationship decision recorded.

principal.description: An access token from /v1/auth/apple, /v1/auth/google or /v1/auth/refresh (PD-030). Opaque; looked up per request; names an account, never a permission. A development server started with THRO_DEV_AUTH=1 accepts X-Thro-Dev-Subject instead.

get.summary: Apple's association file for this host
get.description: webcredentials for the configured app ids, so iOS offers passkeys for this relying party. 404 when no app id is configured.

get.summary: Liveness, the schema version the database stands at, and which code is answering
get.description: Unauthenticated. Reports the migration ledger's current version; a database the code cannot serve is a 503. Also the newest migration this code carries (codeVersion) and the commit it was built from where the host names one (commit), so a deploy can tell the new API from the one it replaced: after a migration both answer at the same schemaVersion (PD-095).

200.description: ok, with schemaVersion, codeVersion and commit

503.description: database unreachable or behind the code

get.summary: This document
get.description: Rendered from the same registry the routes are mounted from.

post.summary: Sign in with Apple
post.description: Verifies Apple's ID token against Apple's published keys, issuer, this app's client id and expiry; creates the account, its player and its claim on first sight (PD-030). The session is THRØ's own.

idToken.description: The provider's ID token (JWT) as the platform SDK returned it.

deviceId.description: This device's stable id; the session family is bound to it.

nonce.description: The nonce the client generated for this sign-in and gave the provider SDK. Required when the token carries one; Apple's token carries its SHA-256, Google's the value.

200.description: a session: accountId, playerId, accessToken (opaque, 15 minutes), refreshToken (single-use, 30 days), accessExpiresAt, created

401.description: the token does not verify, and why

429.description: too many attempts from this address or device; Retry-After says when

503.description: Sign in with Apple is not configured on this server

post.summary: Sign in with Google
post.description: As for Apple, against Google's published keys and issuers.

idToken.description: The provider's ID token (JWT) as the platform SDK returned it.

deviceId.description: This device's stable id; the session family is bound to it.

nonce.description: The nonce the client generated for this sign-in and gave the provider SDK. Required when the token carries one; Apple's token carries its SHA-256, Google's the value.

200.description: a session: accountId, playerId, accessToken (opaque, 15 minutes), refreshToken (single-use, 30 days), accessExpiresAt, created

401.description: the token does not verify, and why

429.description: too many attempts from this address or device; Retry-After says when

503.description: Sign in with Google is not configured on this server

post.summary: End this session family
post.description: Revokes the family the presented access token belongs to; its access and refresh tokens stop working.

post.summary: Sign in with a passkey
post.description: Verifies the assertion — challenge, origin, relying party, user verification, sign count, signature over authenticator data and client data hash — and opens a session for the credential's account.

200.description: a session: accountId, playerId, accessToken (opaque, 15 minutes), refreshToken (single-use, 30 days), accessExpiresAt, created

401.description: the assertion does not verify, and why

429.description: too many attempts from this address or device; Retry-After says when

503.description: passkeys are not configured on this server

post.summary: Begin signing in with a passkey
post.description: Returns the WebAuthn request options (challenge, relying party id, user verification required). Discoverable credentials: no username is asked for.

429.description: too many attempts from this address or device; Retry-After says when

503.description: passkeys are not configured on this server

post.summary: Finish creating a passkey
post.description: Verifies the client data (type, challenge, origin) and the authenticator data (relying party, user presence and verification, credential and COSE key); stores the public key; opens a session. The attestation statement is not verified: THRØ asks for none.

200.description: a session: accountId, playerId, accessToken (opaque, 15 minutes), refreshToken (single-use, 30 days), accessExpiresAt, created

401.description: the registration does not verify, and why

429.description: too many attempts from this address or device; Retry-After says when

503.description: passkeys are not configured on this server

post.summary: Begin creating a passkey
post.description: Returns the WebAuthn creation options (challenge, relying party, user handle, ES256/RS256, resident key and user verification required, attestation none). With a bearer token the passkey is added to that account; without one the registration creates an account. The challenge lives five minutes and is spent once.

429.description: too many attempts from this address or device; Retry-After says when

503.description: passkeys are not configured on this server

post.summary: Rotate a refresh token
post.description: A refresh token is single-use: this marks it used and issues a new pair. Presenting a used token is reuse — a copy exists — and revokes the whole session family (ADR-008).

200.description: a session: accountId, playerId, accessToken (opaque, 15 minutes), refreshToken (single-use, 30 days), accessExpiresAt, created

401.description: unknown, expired, or reused (the family is now revoked)

429.description: too many attempts from this address or device; Retry-After says when

get.summary: The accounts you have blocked (PD-050)
get.description: Ids only: a block list names nobody it does not have to, and the phone already knows who it asked to block. Lifted blocks are not in it.

post.summary: Ask not to be reached by an account (PD-050)
post.description: No reason is asked for and none is stored. Neither account can invite, befriend, claim a seat against or watch the other while it stands. Blocking twice is blocking once.

delete.description: The row is kept and marked lifted; blocking again later is a new block.

post.summary: The one command endpoint (ADR-007)
post.description: Every client-to-server state change, online or from a queue. Identity comes from the principal, the device from X-Thro-Device. Applied is 200; a replay returns what it returned; stale is 409 with the current row; a refusal is 422 in the store's words; a sequence gap is 409; a match the caller is not in is 404.

schema.description: One command. `type` selects the shape; the caller's identity is the authenticated principal and is never read from the body; the device is the X-Thro-Device header.

commandId.description: Idempotency key per device: a replay returns the stored response verbatim.

deviceSeq.description: RecordVisit: the device's gapless sequence for this match.

to.description: RenameTeam: the new name. RearrangeFixture: the new date-time.

players.description: NameLineup: the side in slot order.

expectedVersion.description: The row version the author last saw; 0 when the row does not exist yet. A different current version is a 409 with the current row.

200.description: applied, or a replay of an earlier answer

404.description: not this match, or not in it

get.summary: Open-entry events that have not started yet, with their venues
get.description: The notice on the pub door: open access only, public venues only, no person on any row. Eligibility, entry counts and whether the caller is in are on /v1/me/discovery.

post.summary: Award a fixture nobody played (PD-055)
post.description: A decision with an actor and a reason, and never a scoreline: inventing one would reward an unplayed match in every leg-difference tie-break beneath it (ADR-012). The award goes to one of the fixture's two teams and says why. It corrects a standing result the same way a scoreline does, by naming it as `supersedes`, because a fixture recorded as played and later awarded is a correction and not a second result (PD-059).

supersedes.description: the outcomeId of the result being corrected

400.description: not a UUID, or no reason given

403.description: you do not administer this league season

409.description: this fixture already has a result, or the one you named is no longer the standing one

post.summary: Record what a fixture finished as (PD-055)
post.description: The legs each side won. **The caller does not choose what kind of result this is — the evidence does.** A fixture with a match scored on THRØ behind it records a played result; one without records the official's declared word, which counts in the table exactly the same and is never evidence for a rating. **Correcting a result is a second decision that supersedes the first, never an edit**: send the standing result's `outcomeId` as `supersedes` and the earlier decision stays on the record with its author. Omit it and a fixture that already has a result answers 409; send one that has itself been superseded since you read it and it answers 409 too, because that is a correction somebody else made and this would silently undo it (PD-059).

supersedes.description: the outcomeId of the result being corrected

200.description: the outcome, saying whether it was played or declared

400.description: not two numbers, or supersedes is not a UUID

403.description: you do not administer this league season

409.description: this fixture already has a result, or the one you named is no longer the standing one

post.summary: Annul a result, leaving the fixture to be replayed (PD-065)
post.description: **Different from correcting one.** A correction says the scoreline was wrong; this says the fixture should not have had a result at all — played under protest, abandoned, ordered again by the league. The annulled decision stays on the record, superseded, and the fixture is open: the table counts it as unplayed and the fixture list shows it as annulled with the reason rather than quietly returning it to the ones still to play, because a result that vanishes without trace is how a league stops trusting its own table. A reason is required and the database has always insisted on one. Send the standing result's `outcomeId` as `supersedes`; a fixture with nothing standing has nothing to annul and answers 409.

400.description: no reason, or supersedes is not a UUID

403.description: you do not administer this league season

409.description: this fixture has no standing result, or the one you named is no longer it

get.summary: The caller's friends
get.description: Display names only: a friend is somebody who told you their name across a table. Newest first.

403.description: the development principal has no account

post.summary: Enter a friend code
post.description: Both become friends and the code is spent. Refusals say why: not a code, unknown, used, expired, your own, already friends.

code.description: eight letters and numbers, case and spaces ignored

403.description: not an adult account

409.description: the code cannot be used, with the sentence to show

429.description: too many codes tried from this address or device; Retry-After says when

post.summary: A friend code for the caller to give somebody in person
post.description: Eight characters, seven days, one use. Only an account that has said it is an adult may make one; an unknown age is refused, not guessed (V028).

403.description: not an adult account, with the sentence to show

post.summary: End a friendship from this side
post.description: Recorded as ended, never deleted. Either side may.

200.description: removed: whether there was one to end

get.summary: The public front of the leagues: seasons, divisions, teams and their home venues
get.description: Public rows only — no person is on any of them. Each league lists its sources and each venue the basis it was connected to its team on (a secretary's word, or an inference from the team's name), because imported data says where it came from (PD-033).

parameters.name: locality
parameters.description: a town or district; case-insensitive substring of the league's locality, optional

post.summary: Start a league on THRØ, with its first season, and run it (PD-100)
post.description: The league, its first season and that season's divisions, together or not at all, and whoever starts it becomes the season's administrator. A league THRØ lists from elsewhere is not this: it already has somebody who runs it, and is run only by the person named for it (PD-053).

visibility.description: private keeps it off the public list: a rehearsal, or not yet public

200.description: the league and its first season

400.description: a name, label, date, division or visibility of the wrong shape

post.summary: Rename a league started on THRØ, take it private or public, or end it (PD-103)
post.description: Only the person who started the league. A private league is off the public list and its name is shown nowhere public; its seasons still run for its organiser. Ending is recorded once and never undone: an ended league keeps and answers for every season it had and takes no more. A league THRØ lists from elsewhere refuses everybody here.

200.description: the league as it now stands

400.description: a name or visibility of the wrong shape

403.description: you did not start this league, or THRØ lists it from elsewhere

post.summary: Open the next season of a league started on THRØ (PD-100)
post.description: Only the person who started the league opens its seasons, and becomes each one's administrator. A league THRØ lists from elsewhere refuses everybody here, and says why.

200.description: the league and the season opened

400.description: a label, date or division of the wrong shape

403.description: you did not start this league, or THRØ lists it from elsewhere

409.description: this league already has a season with that label

post.summary: Send a match this phone scored to THRØ (PD-040)
post.description: The device's journal as it wrote it — every visit and every retraction, in deviceSeq order — rather than a replayed total, because a screen that shows a struck row and a server that never heard of it are two accounts of one night. Idempotent by (match, device, deviceSeq): the same upload twice is the same rows, and a phone that lost signal half way sends the lot again. The other seat becomes a competitor THRØ holds no name for, claimable later by a code. The match is recorded self-reported: one player's word until the other confirms it (PD-011). A match that ended short (PD-016) is sent as it ended: its retirement or abandonment is the last row, and nothing is added after it (V034).

seat.description: Which seat the caller sat in. The other is minted.

kind.description: An ending — retirement or abandonment — is the last row when there is one.

seat.description: The seat that threw; for a retirement, the seat that retired. An abandonment names nobody and may leave it out.

200.description: what was stored, and what was already held

post.summary: Enter a match code: the seat it was made for becomes the caller's
post.description: Recorded as a seat claim (V037) and nothing else: the match, and the evidence under it, stay exactly as they were written. Refusals say why — not a code, unknown, used, expired, your own, already in the match, the seat already taken. Rationed per address and per device, like every route that takes a code.

code.description: eight letters and numbers; case, spaces and dashes ignored

200.description: the match, as the caller now reads it

422.description: the code cannot be used, with the sentence to show

429.description: too many codes tried from this address or device; Retry-After says when

get.summary: A match the caller played in
get.description: Both seats — a name only where identity.player_may_be_disclosed allows — the legs as the engine replays the record with struck visits left out, how it ended, who won, which seat sent it, each seat's answer where it still stands, and its standing: self-reported, confirmed, disputed, or recorded for a match scored on THRØ as it was played. Derived from the log on every read and stored nowhere. Anyone not in the match is answered 404.

404.description: not a match the caller played in

post.summary: The other player's answer for a result they did not send
post.description: agree true confirms the result and false contests it, appended to the trust stream as ResultConfirmed or ResultContested naming the seat (V037). Every answer is kept and the latest stands — but only for the record it answered: when the sender sends more of the match, the other player is asked again. The player who sent a match cannot answer for it, because their word is the match, and an abandoned match has no result to confirm. The phone names itself in X-Thro-Device.

agree.description: true confirms the result, false contests it

200.description: the match, with the answer counted

404.description: not a match the caller played in

409.description: the answer could not be recorded; try again

post.summary: A code for the other seat of a match the caller sent (PD-043)
post.description: Eight characters, seven days, one use. The sender gives it to the player they played, who enters it on their own phone to take the other seat. Only the player who sent the match may make one, only for a match sent from a phone, and only while the other seat is nobody's; asking again while a code is live hands back the same code rather than a second one.

404.description: not a match the caller sent

422.description: no code can be made for it, in words

delete.summary: Erase my account and everything that identifies me
delete.description: Destroys the display name, every Apple, Google and passkey credential, every session on every device, the device labels, live friendships, the claim on the competitor row and the consent record. Keeps the matches played, because a match is the other player's record too and a league's table stands on it — and after this those rows carry a competitor id that resolves to no person (V031, the shape V018 set). Cannot be undone; signing in again makes a new account. The caller's session is dead the moment this returns.

get.summary: Who am I
get.description: The caller's account id, player id, display name (and whether they have set one), and age band. Carries the terms in force and whether this account has accepted them (PD-050), so the phone can hold somebody at the agreement before their first public word without a second request to find out.

post.summary: Say whether you may be named
post.description: Two separate answers (PD-088). `listing` is being named on your team's public page; `live` is being named on a screen while you are playing, which says where you are at the time and is therefore asked for on its own. Only for yourself: a guardian's consent is recorded by a named person through the secretary, never by a caller asserting it here. Saying no revokes and keeps the record, so what somebody agreed to and when is answerable. `live` is refused for anyone not recorded as an adult, with the sentence to show them.

200.description: scope, given, and why not when it was refused

403.description: the development principal has no account

get.summary: Darts the caller can play, and why each card is there
get.description: The discovery read model for the caller between from and to. Every card carries its reasons; nothing is called eligible that THRØ cannot check.

get.summary: The caller's own Secretary tasks, by section
get.description: Tasks whose subject is the caller: consent, claims, anything the Secretary needs from them.

get.summary: The matches the caller played in, newest first
get.description: Sent by the caller, or taken with a code; at most thirty, each in the shape GET /v1/matches/{matchId} answers.

put.description: A name is the person's to give; it is never taken from a provider's token on their behalf.

ageBand.description: Self-declared, once asked. Never back to unknown. What unlocks friends (V028) is adult.

contactEmail.description: PD-104: an organiser's contact email — an adult who runs a league or a team. Empty takes it away. 403 for anybody else, with why.

get.summary: The league seasons you administer (PD-100)
get.description: Newest first, with the league's name, so an organiser can find their way back to the season they run.

get.summary: The teams the caller is in
get.description: Current memberships only, newest first, with the caller's role and the member count.

post.summary: Accept the terms (PD-050)
post.description: Recorded once per version, with the version accepted, because that is the only honest answer to what somebody agreed to. Accepting a version twice changes nothing.

get.summary: What is waiting to be answered (PD-050)
get.description: The moderation queue: unanswered first, then a report raised by or about a child, then by the hour its answer is due. Open only to the accounts named at boot as answering reports — THRØ has no staff table, and a queue anyone could read is a queue that tells people they were reported.

200.description: the queue, each report with its reason and when it is due

403.description: not one of the people who answer reports

post.summary: Report something somebody wrote (PD-050)
post.description: A team, venue or league name, an account, or a match. Names the thing and a sentence of reason; the answer is due within a day, and a report raised by or about a child goes to the front of the queue.

200.description: the report, with when it is answered by

400.description: not something THRØ can report, or no reason given

post.summary: Answer a report (PD-050)
post.description: A decision is a row of its own, so a second look is a second decision and never an edit of the first. Nothing a player wrote is destroyed by one: it is left, hidden or corrected, or the account is suspended, and the note says why.

400.description: not one of the answers a report can have, or no note given

403.description: not one of the people who answer reports

post.summary: Accept a team into a league season (PD-053)
post.description: Applied becomes accepted, and never the other way back. Only an accepted team is a row in the season's table, so this is the act that puts a side in the league. The caller must administer the season: a league administrator is named, never self-appointed, so a server where nobody has been named refuses everybody.

403.description: you do not administer this league season

409.description: that team is not waiting to be accepted

get.summary: A league season's fixtures, played and still to play (PD-056)
get.description: The other half of a league's own data: the table says how the season stands, this says what is left. Each fixture carries its date, its lifecycle — scheduled, rearranged, postponed — the venue, and what it finished as where it has: played, declared by an official, awarded or walked over. Read from the same rows the table is, so the two cannot disagree. Public means public: a team or venue marked private is not named, though the fixture is still listed, because hiding it would leave a hole in a league's own calendar.

post.summary: Give a league season its fixtures (PD-099)
post.description: A list of fixtures, written together or not at all: one that cannot be played refuses the list and says which. Each is between two teams the league has **accepted** into this season — a team still waiting is not in the league, and a fixture it played would count in nobody's table — in the same division, on a day inside the season's dates as they fall in the UK. The division may be omitted, and is then the teams' own. The venue is the home team's at the time of the fixture, and is frozen on it. A fixture already scheduled between the same teams at the same moment is a 409, so sending a list twice does not play every match twice.

400.description: not a list of fixtures, or a field of the wrong shape

403.description: you do not administer this league season

409.description: a fixture in the list is already scheduled

422.description: a fixture in the list cannot be played, and which

get.summary: The games in play in this season, for a screen in the room (PD-088)
get.description: Every match with a visit in it and no outcome yet: the two teams, the venue, the legs, the remainders and whose throw it is. A player is **named only** where `identity.player_may_be_shown_live` allows — an adult who has said yes, and nobody else; a minor and an unknown age are both null, never a placeholder. A private team is unnamed and its game is still listed. Needs no account, because the screen it is for has nobody signed in to it.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: at most this many, default 20, capped at 20

get.summary: How to reach the people running a league season (PD-104)
get.description: The contact emails the season's administrators chose to give, for the admins of teams accepted into the season and for the administrators themselves. Nobody else, and never public. An organiser who gave none is not on the list, and a season whose organisers gave none answers an empty list rather than an invented one.

403.description: you neither run this season nor a team in it

get.summary: A league season's table, computed from the results under it (PD-054)
get.description: Derived on every read from each fixture's live outcome and the league's own approved points policy. Nothing is stored, so a table cannot drift from the results beneath it, be edited into disagreeing with them, or be left behind by a correction. Only teams the league affiliated are rows: a team that merely says it plays in the league (PD-049) never is. An awarded fixture or a walkover moves the points and never the legs, so a match nobody played cannot pollute a leg-difference tie-break. Every row says which step of the declared chain separated it from the one below, and every table says whose rules ordered it — the league's own, or THRØ's standard of two a win and one a draw, named as the standard so nobody mistakes it for their league's constitution.

parameters.name: division
parameters.description: a division of this season; omitted gives every division

200.description: the table, by division, with the rules it was ordered under

409.description: this league's own points rules name something THRØ cannot apply, and say what

get.summary: A league season as its administrator runs it: its dates, divisions and every team that asked in (PD-099)
get.description: Waiting and accepted alike, each with the division it asked for and the affiliationId that accepting it needs. The public fixture list and table show only what the league has decided; this is the season before that, so it is for the season's administrator alone. A season nobody has is a 404 whoever asks, so a mistyped address does not read as a refusal.

200.description: the season, its divisions and its teams

403.description: you do not administer this league season

post.summary: Add a team to a league season, in it at once (PD-100)
post.description: The league letting a team in itself, so there is no application to accept. The team is a listed one that nobody runs yet. In a season with divisions it names one of them.

200.description: the team, accepted into the season

400.description: no name, or divisionId is not a UUID

403.description: you do not administer this league season

409.description: the season already has a team with that name

422.description: the division is not this season's, or none was named

get.summary: A match's evidence, live (ADR-007)
get.description: text/event-stream. Every event of the match in commit order, then each new one as it commits; the event id is `match:{matchId}:{commitXid}-{seq}` and a reconnect with Last-Event-ID replays from there. A comment ping every 15 seconds; a client that has seen nothing for 45 seconds treats the stream as stale. Open to the match's participants, holders of a scoring grant for it, and officials of its event — there is no spectator stream yet.

403.description: not in this match

post.summary: Start a team
post.description: The caller becomes its first member and admin (team#admin). Plan §6, row one.

post.summary: Enter a team code
post.description: The caller becomes a member, as a player. Refusals say why: not a code, unknown, expired, full, already in.

409.description: the code cannot be used, with the sentence to show

429.description: too many codes tried from this address or device; Retry-After says when

get.summary: A team's front
get.description: Name, locality, home venue, the seasons it is in, and its roster — names only where identity.player_may_be_disclosed allows, everyone else counted and not named. A private team answers 404 to anyone not in it. With a bearer, yourRole says what you are in it, and the team's admin also sees each roster entry's memberId, to name a captain with (PD-045).

404.description: no such team, or not yours to see

post.summary: Say a listed league team is yours, and run it on THRØ (PD-047)
post.description: For a team read out of a league's pages that nobody on THRØ runs. The caller becomes its admin by their own say, and the team's front says that is what happened. Adults only, and an age nobody has said is not adult. A team somebody already runs is joined with their code instead.

409.description: it cannot be taken on, with the sentence to show

post.summary: Set the team's home venue
post.description: An existing public venue by venueId, or a new one by name and locality. Admin or captain only. A change closes the old tenure and opens the new; nothing is overwritten.

400.description: neither a venue nor a name

403.description: not the admin or captain

get.summary: A team's Secretary inbox, for those who run it
get.description: Requires team.manage on the team (admin or captain). Anyone else is 403, and the refusal is on the audit record.

403.description: you do not run this team

post.summary: A team code to give the side
post.description: Eight characters, thirty days, up to twenty people. Admin or captain only (V029).

403.description: not the admin or captain, with the sentence to show

post.summary: Say which league the team plays in (PD-049)
post.description: The team's admin or captain says the team plays in a league THRØ lists. It is carried as their say and never as the league's listing: a league's divisions are filled from the league's own published pages and from nothing else. Saying it twice is saying it once.

403.description: not the team's admin or captain

404.description: THRØ lists no league like that

delete.summary: Stop saying the team plays in that league (PD-049)
delete.description: Marked withdrawn and kept, never deleted: who said their team played there, and when, stays readable.

403.description: not the team's admin or captain

post.summary: Name the captain or vice-captain, or make somebody a player again (PD-045)
post.description: Admin only. One captain and one vice-captain at a time: naming one when there is one makes the old one a player. A change ends the membership row and opens another — who captained the side is the team's history (V014) — and the captain's team.manage relation is granted and revoked with it. memberId is the roster entry's own handle, which the team's front shows to its admin alone.

200.description: the team's front, as its admin reads it

403.description: not the team's admin, with the sentence to show

get.summary: Public venues by name
get.description: For a captain choosing a home: name contains q, optionally in a locality; at most twenty.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: part of the venue's name, required
